newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish rates rise on c.bank revrepo, NBP-bill sale.
newsitem.headline: Polish rates rise on c.bank revrepo, NBP-bill sale.

text.p: The Polish money market's main 14-day drainage maximum rate rebounded 0.10 point to 19.05 percent at Wednesday's National Bank of Poland (NBP) auction, pulling up money market rates and secondary T-bill yields.

Dealers said today's 1.47 billion zloty reverse repo coupled with a 990 million zloty NBP-bill sale drained most of the surplus cash from the overliquid market and gave players sought after high-yielding longer-term paper.
"Both T-bill yields and money market rates rose as the 14-day drainage rate rose and the NBP sold its bills at an attractive price," said Wojciech Kolalczyk of Bank Handlowy SA.

Dealers said today's rise in the 14-day reverse repo rate, the first since May 22, showed that the NBP was adhering to its monetary policy plan, which concentrates on controlling money supply aggregates and allows short-term rate fluctuations.

"Volatility of one-day depos is likely to remain high in line with the NBP's policy, but longer deposits are likely to stabilise around 19 percent after today's drainage," said Krzysztof Czarkowski from BRE SA.
Overnight rates rose to 17.0/18.5 percent from 15.0/17.5 percent at 0650 GMT and 12.5/16.2 on Tuesday. Tomorrow/next were at 17.5/19.0 percent, up from Tuesday's 13.0/16.45.

The central bank sold 182-day and 273-day NBP-bills at an average yield of 19.61 percent and 19.74 percent respectively, about half a point above comparable yields in early trade on the secondary T-bill market.
On the secondary market, 52-week T-bills sold on Monday were traded around 19.45 percent, up from 19.20 this morning, and nearly flat from an average primary yield of 19.46 percent.
Dealers said nine-month T-bills were traded around 19.35 percent and half-year paper was at 19.25 percent up 0.20 point from this morning's and Tusday's levels.

The zloty closed softer at 1.74/1.67 percent from the trading band centre from Tuesday's 1.77/1.71 percent after banks cought on to a currency-buying trend likely sparked by a large domestic client order, dealers said.
"The currency buying was mostly speculative but it may have been originated by a large client order," said Pawel Gajewski from Creditanstalt in Warsaw.
The zloty was at 2.7360/70 per dollar, down from 2.7275/05 on Tuesday and at 1.8505/25 per mark, just down from 1.8500/20.
